readerContract.humanQuestion: I have ChatGPT Pro $200, or was considering it. What can I do during the sign-up pause without accidentally losing the tier I already have?
readerContract.promisedPayoff: Know which new sign-ups and upgrades are paused, what remains available, and the limited actions the Help Center says keep or end an active Pro $200 subscription.
readerContract.priorKnowledge: No subscription vocabulary, plan history, or knowledge of OpenAI’s tiers is assumed.
readerContract.centralMentalModel: A plan pause changes who can newly enter or move into a tier; it does not automatically remove an active subscription. A cancellation or completed downgrade is a separate account change with its own consequence.
readerContract.dailyLifeConnection: A reader is deciding whether to change, cancel, or continue an existing subscription.
readerContract.surfaceJob: A short September 12 consumer notice about OpenAI’s September 10 Pro $200 sign-up and upgrade pause, not a product review or capacity analysis.
readerContract.desiredFeeling: I can tell whether an official rule concerns a planned account change or an already-ended plan.

canonicalTruth.owner: OpenAI owns the current plan rules; Computerworld independently reports the announced pause; NewsStand only explains the stated subscriber choices.
canonicalTruth.freshnessTrigger: Reopen the Help Center before publication or if OpenAI changes eligibility, cancellation, renewal, downgrade, price, or pause status.

candidateRepairPreflight.scope: Only new sign-ups and upgrades to Pro $200 / Pro 20X are paused.
candidateRepairPreflight.existing: Existing Pro $200 subscriptions continue to renew as usual.
candidateRepairPreflight.lapse: Once Pro $200 ends after cancellation, completed downgrade, or unresolved renewal failure, the Help Center says it cannot be repurchased until the pause lifts.
candidateRepairPreflight.hundred: Pro $100 remains available to upgrade into.
candidateRepairPreflight.nonClaims: No stated end date, capacity metric, API, Business, Enterprise, price, or service-quality claim.

draftArchitecture.plainAnswer: OpenAI says new sign-ups and upgrades to ChatGPT Pro $200 are temporarily paused. Existing $200 subscriptions continue; Pro $100 remains available; and a lapsed $200 subscription cannot be repurchased until the pause lifts.
causalSequence: A person first checks whether she is already on Pro $200 or is trying to enter it.
The pause blocks a new Pro $200 purchase or upgrade, but does not by itself cancel an active Pro $200 subscription.
A cancellation, completed downgrade, refund that ends the subscription, or unresolved renewal failure can end Pro $200.
After it ends, OpenAI says the reader cannot repurchase Pro $200 until the pause lifts.
draftArchitecture.workedCase: A reader who schedules a cancellation still has Pro $200 through the current billing cycle; the Help Center distinguishes that from a cancellation that has taken effect.
draftArchitecture.transferCase: Someone considering a new upgrade has a different question: OpenAI says new moves into Pro $200 are paused, while Pro $100 remains available.
draftArchitecture.usefulAction: Before changing or canceling Pro $200, read the pause FAQ and distinguish a scheduled change from one that has taken effect.
draftArchitecture.formatSpecificStructure: The Story; The LAiDIES Read; What This Means for You; Cocktail Party; Class Notes.
draftArchitecture.antiTemplateDecision: Lead with the subscriber decision rather than infrastructure speculation. Explain the state change with one active-subscriber case and one new-plan case; omit capacity, launch, API, and work-product claims.

discoveryChecks.question: Can any Californian use the finished AskCA assistant today?
discoveryChecks.answer: No. Sign-ups are open to eligible adult California residents, and the current official page says pilot participants will explore it in October.

discoveryChecks.question: Does searching official sources guarantee AskCA is right?
discoveryChecks.answer: No. California’s own About and conditions pages say the prototype may be wrong or outdated and important information should be checked with the actual agency.

discoveryChecks.question: Is the September 30 CalCareers feature the same event as the AskCA October pilot?
discoveryChecks.answer: No. The state describes it as a separate first departmental pilot powered by the same engine.

representativeProofPlan.highestRisk: A reader may mistake a paused new purchase for an automatic loss of active access, or make a cancellation that ends her access.
representativeProofPlan.plannedProof: Map each visitor-facing plan rule to the Help Center and run the producer and prose validators against exact candidate bytes.
representativeProofPlan.acceptanceOutcome: A reader can identify whether she is already subscribed, seeking an upgrade, or considering an ending change, without any unstated forecast or product claim.
